solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stay on edge

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a business letter's subject line
a side is an edge or border of something

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remain perched on the brink of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to live or dwell there, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Seaside resort one favoured for special treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside resort on the North Yorkshire coast in England
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A holiday town is singled out as a favourite for VIP handling.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for welcoming someone with lavish ceremony.

clue.text: Strongboxes commandos lined with iron

indicators.note: lined with means having something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment of commandos
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Elite troops' strongboxes are reinforced with metal plating.
explanation.definitionFit: Safes are lockable steel containers for valuables.

clue.text: Get rid of much of cold that's upset friend

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: iced means chilled or cold
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Someone sheds most of a chill that has upset a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb once meant killing one in ten, and now means destroying a large proportion.

clue.text: Dating drunk drinking fashionable cocktail

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece swallows the other
drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters of dating are scrambled

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A date goes badly as someone gets tipsy on a trendy mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dating drunk' reads as a tipsy couple, but 'drunk' is the anagram signal and 'drinking' the container; Gin and It is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin and It is a classic mixed drink of gin and Italian vermouth, an example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Mixed peel with mint in? Try with sauce

indicators.note: mixed suggests ingredients stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: candied peel and mint stirred in, served with a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks culinary, but it means cheek, so 'with sauce' means cheekily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is old slang for cheek or insolence, so acting with it is acting rudely.

clue.text: Queen with extremely awful temper

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the word awful

explanation.surface: A monarch flies into a terrible rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' reads as anger, but here it is the verb meaning to toughen metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal glass or metal is to heat and cool it slowly to toughen it, like tempering.

clue.text: Showing bust firm left beset by strike

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: to strike out text is to delete it
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company left out of pocket by industrial action goes bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like financial failure; it is the bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut neckline leaves the neck and shoulders and top of the bosom exposed.

clue.text: Flirted with you once in turning point

indicators.note: in places the old pronoun inside
turning means the letters for point are read in reverse

parts.note: a dot is a point
ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Someone once trifled with you at a pivotal moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with someone is to play with their affections, as a flirt does.

clue.text: Really hot cafe, door guards going around

indicators.note: going around means turning back, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
the clue words guard the answer, holding it inside them across their word breaks

explanation.surface: A scorching café has its door watched by bouncers patrolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'door guards' looks like bouncers; in fact 'guards' says the letters hOT CAFE Door hold the answer, and 'going around' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in actual fact or in reality, as opposed to officially.

clue.text: Men helping to defend box and scoring

indicators.note: to defend means to surround something protectively, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers in the army
a ration is a helping or share
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: Players have to protect the goal area while trying to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoring' looks like a sporting term, but it means writing music for an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing out a piece for the instruments of an ensemble is arranging, or scoring, it.

clue.text: Nervous when there's wages about to steal

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: pay is wages
to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Someone is jittery on payday because they plan to pocket the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and being prone to sudden alarm are near synonyms.

clue.text: Starts off at seven in the morning, after small tea

indicators.note: after places the morning piece behind the letter for small
the starts of the words at and seven are taken, one letter from each

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone rises at seven a.m. and has a little cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black variety grown in north-east India.

clue.text: Dog with dog lead evenly trimmed

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

indicators.note: evenly takes the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, of the word lead

explanation.surface: A dog on a lead has had its coat neatly clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut short or reduced has been trimmed back.

clue.text: Artificial part of expert's argument

parts.note: a pro is an expert; with the apostrophe s, pro's
a thesis is an argument put forward

explanation.surface: Part of a specialist's case seems contrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial part' reads like a judgement on the argument, but it defines a replacement body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is a manufactured replacement for a missing limb or organ.

clue.text: One who's experienced love, great LSD trips

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: trips suggests stumbling about, so the letters of great and LSD are rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran hippy recalls romance and wild acid trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' plays on acid trips but is the anagram signal; LSD also once meant pounds, shillings and pence.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long practised at something.

clue.text: Broadcast live in two different ways

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
live is read a second way, as the first-person form am, as in I am

explanation.surface: A transmission goes out live, in two separate formats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is used twice: once as BE and again as AM, both forms of the verb meaning to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam a signal is to transmit or broadcast it.

clue.text: Mechanic's unfortunate bad luck

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things going wrong, so the letters of mechanic's are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A car repairer suffers a run of bad fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is an unlucky accident or misfortune.

clue.text: Papers turning a pallid colour in refuse

indicators.note: turning means the letters for papers are read backwards

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are papers
sallow is a sickly yellowish pallor

explanation.surface: Documents going pale yellow are thrown out as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like the noun meaning rubbish; it is the verb meaning reject.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow a claim or goal is to reject it or refuse to permit it.

clue.text: Fuss excessively, hosting duke

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: Someone makes too much of an aristocrat coming to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Rows in southern river, showing determination

indicators.note: in places the rows piece inside the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Rowers out on a river in the south show grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' tempts as rowing, but it means lines; the Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hardness of resolve, the quality of firm determination.

clue.text: Community around London's West End, reluctant to come forward

indicators.note: around means the shy piece wraps round the other

parts.note: coy means shy, reluctant to put oneself forward

indicators.note: the west end of an across word is its left half, so the first half of London is taken

explanation.surface: A shy group gathers in central London's theatreland.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district; here it means the left-hand half of the word London.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a settled group of people living together, a community.

clue.text: Foremost of adventurers travelling to Saturn?

definitions.text: Foremost of adventurers travelling to Saturn?

indicators.note: foremost of takes the leading letter of the word adventurers
travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of to Saturn are rearranged

explanation.surface: The leading explorer heads off on a space voyage to the ringed planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a space traveller heading for Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller is exactly who would make a journey to another planet.

clue.text: Help when ready

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: Assistance arrives when everything is prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful, a help or benefit.

clue.text: Teeming area with wood

parts.note: ash is a type of wood

explanation.surface: A region is described as thick with forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded or overflowing with something, so teeming.

clue.text: Clergyman dismissing his first offence

indicators.note: dismissing his first means the clergyman loses his first letter

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is sacked for his first misdemeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Tough soldiers, retreating Roman men

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: iron means tough, as in an iron will
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Hardened troops fall back in the face of Roman legionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural for gentlemen, so men in Rome.

clue.text: Russian politician still to admit large crime

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet to come
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: A Russian leader has still to own up to a major offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Hanging around with sailor and Yankee in band

parts.note: tar is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: in places the Yankee letter inside the band

parts.note: a ring is a band
Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: A seaman and an American loiter with a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering or delaying somewhere is tarrying.

clue.text: Pair with say back pain

parts.note: a twin is one of a pair, or one paired with another

indicators.note: back means the letters for say are read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say also signals

explanation.surface: Someone together with a partner suffers backache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back pain' reads as one ailment, but 'back' reverses EG and 'pain' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pain.
